questions.question_text: Find the conversion cost from the following information: Material Consumed Rs. 10000; Labour Rs. 6000; Fuel used to operate the machine Rs. 2000; Other factory Expenses Rs. 1000; Advertisement Rs. 5000; Distribution Rs. 2000; Other Administrative Expenses Rs. 1000
questions.explanation:
Conversion Cost = Direct Labour + Manufacturing Overheads.
Direct Labour = Rs. 6000.
Manufacturing Overheads = Fuel (Rs. 2000) + Other factory expenses (Rs. 1000) = Rs. 3000.
Conversion Cost = 6000 + 3000 = Rs. 9000.
Note: Advertisement, Distribution, and Administrative expenses are period costs and not included in conversion cost.

questions.question_text: Find the cost of goods manufactured from the following information: Raw Material opening stock Rs.2000; Raw Material Purchased during the period Rs. 10000; Closing Raw Material Rs. 1000; Factory Labour Rs. 5000; Other Factory Expenses Rs. 6000; Opening WIP Rs. 3000; Closing WIP Rs. 2000; Selling and Distribution Expenses Rs. 5000; Admin Exp. Rs. 2000
questions.explanation:
Cost of Goods Manufactured (COGM) calculation:
Raw Material Consumed = Opening Stock (2000) + Purchases (10000) - Closing Stock (1000) = 11000.
Prime Cost = RM Consumed (11000) + Factory Labour (5000) = 16000.
Gross Factory Cost = Prime Cost (16000) + Other Factory Expenses (6000) = 22000.
COGM = Gross Factory Cost (22000) + Opening WIP (3000) - Closing WIP (2000) = 23000.
Selling, Distribution, and Admin expenses are period costs and ignored for COGM.

questions.question_text: Alpha Limited Budgeted Factory Overhead for the year was Rs. 100000; The budgeted Machine hour is 1000 hours for the year. The factory worked for 800 hours and incurred a factory overhead of Rs. 120000. Find the under-recovery or over-recovery of Factory Overhead for the year.
questions.explanation:
Standard Overhead Rate = Budgeted Overhead / Budgeted Machine Hours = 100000 / 1000 = Rs. 100 per hour.
Recovered (Applied) Overhead = Actual Hours × Standard Rate = 800 × 100 = Rs. 80000.
Actual Overhead Incurred = Rs. 120000.
Under-recovery = Actual Overhead - Recovered Overhead = 120000 - 80000 = Rs. 40000.

questions.question_text: A client of Star Carpentary asked to give a quote to produce 100 units of Chairs. The Cost Accountant estimates the following expenses: Wood Rs. 50000; Paint and other material Rs. 20000; Labour Rs. 40000; Factory Overhead Rs. 10000; Allocated Administrative overhead Rs. 1000; Transport Expense Rs. 10000. Find the cost per unit of Chair.
questions.explanation:
Total Estimated Cost Calculation:
Wood (50000) + Paint/Material (20000) + Labour (40000) + Factory Overhead (10000) + Admin Overhead (1000) + Transport (10000) = Rs. 131000.
Cost per unit = Total Cost / Number of Units = 131000 / 100 = Rs. 1310.

questions.question_text: Compute the cost per Equivalent Unit for the conversion cost from the information given below: Conversion Cost in Opening WIP: Rs. 3000; Conversion cost incurred during the period: Rs. 13440; Opening WIP Units (60% completed on conversion cost): 100 units; New Units introduced during the period: 3000 units; Closing WIP: 600 units (40% complted on conversion cost).
questions.explanation:
Using the Weighted Average Method:
Total Units to Account for = Opening WIP (100) + New Units Introduced (3000) = 3100.
Completed Units = Total Units - Closing WIP = 3100 - 600 = 2500 units.
Equivalent Units (EU) for Conversion Cost = (Completed Units × 100%) + (Closing WIP × 40%) = 2500 + (600 × 40%) = 2500 + 240 = 2740 EU.
Total Conversion Cost = Opening WIP Cost + Cost Incurred = 3000 + 13440 = 16440.
Cost per Equivalent Unit = 16440 / 2740 = 6.00.

questions.question_text: Compute the number of completed units for the month from the information given below: Opening WIP Units (100% completed on Material and 60% completed on conversion cost): 100 units; New Units introduced during the period: 3000 units; Closing WIP: 600 units (100% completed on Material and 40% complted on conversion cost).
questions.explanation:
Total Units Input = Opening WIP + New Units Introduced = 100 + 3000 = 3100 units.
Total Units Output = Completed Units + Closing WIP.
3100 = Completed Units + 600.
Completed Units = 3100 - 600 = 2500 units.

questions.question_text: Compute the cost per Equivalent Unit for the conversion cost from the information given below: Conversion Cost in Opening WIP: Rs. 3000; Conversion cost incurred during the period: Rs. 13440; Opening WIP Units (60% completed on conversion cost): 100 units; New Units introduced during the period: 3000 units; Closing WIP: 600 units (40% complted on conversion cost); Units completed: 2400 units. Normal Loss: 100 units
questions.explanation:
Using the Weighted Average Method:
Equivalent Units (EU) = (Completed Units × 100%) + (Closing WIP × 40%) + Normal Loss.
Normal loss is absorbed by good units and has 0 Equivalent Units for cost spread.
Total EU = 2400 + (600 × 40%) + 0 = 2400 + 240 = 2640 EU.
Total Conversion Cost = Opening WIP Cost + Cost Incurred = 3000 + 13440 = 16440.
Cost per EU = 16440 / 2640 = 6.227 = 6.23.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the most appropriate cost driver for the material handling department?
questions.explanation: Material handling activities are driven by the movement and physical transportation of batches or shipments rather than just machine hours or direct material cost. Therefore, the number of shipments acts as the most logical batch-level cost driver.

questions.question_text: CleanTech manufacturers 3 models of washing machines. The design department spent Rs. 5,00,000 during the year. You have the following information: Production Quantity: 3000 units of Model X; 5000 units of Model Y; 10000 units of Model Z. Number of Designs: 300 for Model X; 150 for Model Y and 50 for Model Z; Assembly Hours per unit: 5 hours for Product X; 3 hours for Product Y and 1 hour for Product Z. How much of the design department cost should be allocated to Product X?
questions.explanation:
Design department costs are driven by the Number of Designs (Activity Based Costing).
Total Designs = 300 (X) + 150 (Y) + 50 (Z) = 500 designs.
Design Cost Allocation Rate = Total Design Cost / Total Designs = 500000 / 500 = Rs. 1000 per design.
Cost allocated to Product X = Designs for X × Rate = 300 × 1000 = Rs. 3,00,000.

questions.question_text: Jupiter Pharma manufactuers about 50 tablets using a set of equipment. The products are manufacturered in batches and the equipment are to be cleaned and calibrated before taking up a new product. Each time when a new tablet is taken up for the production, the company spends Rs. 1,00,000 towards cleaning and calibration cost. The cleaning and calibration activity is:
questions.explanation: Cleaning and calibration occur every time a new production run is set up, regardless of the number of individual tablets produced within that specific run. This aligns perfectly with a Batch-level Activity in the Activity Based Costing hierarchy.

questions.question_text: A multi-product electronic company spends Rs. 50 cr. per year for advertisement. Advertisement is a
questions.explanation: Advertising generally promotes specific product lines or models across a market. It supports an entire product's life cycle rather than just individual units or isolated production batches, making it a Product-Level Activity.

questions.question_text: A toothpaste manufacturer sells each 50 grams packet for Rs. 70. The cost structure shows the following: Material: Rs. 25; Labour Rs. 3; Other manufacturing expenses: Rs. 2; Fixed cost for the period is Rs. 20,00,000. How many units the company has to produce and sell to achieve a target profit of Rs. 50 lakhs?
questions.explanation:
Selling Price per unit = Rs. 70
Variable Cost per unit = Material (25) + Labour (3) + Other mfg expenses (2) = Rs. 30
Contribution Margin per unit = Sales - Variable Cost = 70 - 30 = Rs. 40
Required Units = (Fixed Cost + Target Profit) / Contribution per unit
Required Units = (20,00,000 + 50,00,000) / 40 = 70,00,000 / 40 = 175,000 units.

questions.question_text: Find the margin of safety from the following information: Break-even Sales: Rs. 10 lakhs; Budgeted Sales: Rs. 130 lakhs; Current Sales: Rs. 120 lakhs; Current Profit: Rs. 40 lakhs.
questions.explanation:
Margin of Safety (MOS) is calculated as the excess of current actual sales over the break-even sales.
MOS = Current Sales - Break-Even Sales
MOS = 120 lakhs - 10 lakhs = Rs. 110 lakhs.

questions.question_text: Sun Corporation is preparing budget for the next year and wants to double the profit. From the information given below, find the price at which the company can double the profit from the current profit of Rs. 10000 to Rs. 20000. Current Selling price per unit: Rs. 10; Current Sales Quantity: 5000 units; Variable Cost per unit: Rs. 4; Fixed Cost: Rs. 20000. Estimated Quantity for the next period: 5000 units.
questions.explanation:
Target Profit = Rs. 20000.
Fixed Cost = Rs. 20000.
Target Contribution Required = Fixed Cost + Target Profit = 20000 + 20000 = Rs. 40000.
Estimated Sales Quantity = 5000 units.
Required Contribution per unit = 40000 / 5000 = Rs. 8.
New Selling Price = Variable Cost per unit + Required Contribution per unit = 4 + 8 = Rs. 12.

questions.question_text: An entity produces 20,000 units of a part which is required for producing product "A". The total production cost of this part is Rs.110,000. It consist of Rs. 70,000 variable cost and Rs.40,000 fixed cost. The management has an offer from an outsider to supply the same parts. If the entity decides to purchase from the outside supplier, it can save only Rs. 10000 fixed cost (balance Rs. 30000 will be still incurred). How much it can offer maximum to the outside supplier?
questions.explanation:
In a Make or Buy decision, the maximum acceptable purchase price equals the total avoidable internal costs.
Avoidable Variable Cost = Rs. 70,000.
Avoidable Fixed Cost = Rs. 10,000.
Total Avoidable Cost = 70,000 + 10,000 = Rs. 80,000.
Maximum offer per unit = Total Avoidable Cost / Number of Units = 80,000 / 20,000 = Rs. 4 per unit.

questions.question_text: Mars Corporation that produces 5 different products using a set of same equipment has surplus machine hours of 20000 hours after meeting the minimum requirement of the customers. If the demand for the products are unlimited, what should be basis on which it should decide to allocate the surplus machine hours?
questions.explanation: When dealing with a limiting factor (scarce resource like machine hours), management should rank and select products based on the Contribution Margin per unit of the limiting factor (in this case, Contribution per machine hour) to maximize total profitability.

questions.question_text: The Degree of Operating Leverage for two products are as follows: Product A: 1.20; Product B: 2.00. If sales are expected to increase by 20% in the next period, which product's profit will increase more?

options.B: Depends on Contribution Margin of the products
options.C: Profit of both products will decline

questions.explanation:
Degree of Operating Leverage (DOL) acts as a multiplier measuring how sensitive profit is to a change in sales.
Percentage Change in Profit = DOL × Percentage Change in Sales.
Product A Profit Increase = 1.20 × 20% = 24%.
Product B Profit Increase = 2.00 × 20% = 40%.
Therefore, Product B's profit will increase more.

questions.question_text: Alpha Ltd is preparing production budget for the month of January. Sales Department wants to have 10% of the next month inventory to handle spurt in demand. Budgeted Sales for January and February are 30000 units and 28000 units respectively. January opening stock is expected to be 500 units. How many units that Production Department has to produce in the month of January?
questions.explanation:
Production Quantity = Budgeted Sales + Desired Closing Stock - Opening Stock
Budgeted Sales (January) = 30000 units.
Desired Closing Stock (January) = 10% of February Sales = 10% × 28000 = 2800 units.
Opening Stock (January) = 500 units.
Production = 30000 + 2800 - 500 = 32300 units.

questions.question_text: Alpha Ltd is preparing Raw Material budget for the month of January. Sales Department wants to have 10% of the next month inventory to handle spurt in demand. Budgeted Sales for January and February are 30000 units and 28000 units respectively. January opening stock is expected to be 500 units. Each unit of product requires 2 KGs of raw materials. Purchase Department would like to have 2000 KGs Raw Material Stock as closing inventory at the end of January. How many units of raw materials that the Purchase Department has to procure for the month of January?
questions.explanation:
First, calculate Production units for January: Sales (30000) + Desired Closing FG Stock (10% of 28000 = 2800) - Opening FG Stock (500) = 32300 units.
Raw Material Required for Production = 32300 units × 2 KGs/unit = 64600 KGs.
Raw Material Purchases = RM for Production + Desired Closing RM Stock - Opening RM Stock.
Assuming Opening RM Stock is 0 (as not provided), Purchases = 64600 + 2000 - 0 = 66600 KGs.

questions.question_text: Alpha Ltd., gives 15 days credit to its customers. Budgeted January Sales is Rs. 5,00,000. Opening Receivables is Rs. 2,00,000. Compute January Cash Collection.
questions.explanation:
A 15 days credit period means that approximately 50% of a month's sales are collected in the month of sale, and the remaining 50% is collected in the subsequent month.
Collection from Opening Receivables = Rs. 2,00,000.
Collection from January Sales = 50% of 5,00,000 = Rs. 2,50,000.
Total Cash Collection = 2,00,000 + 2,50,000 = Rs. 4,50,000.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Cash budget integrates all financial budgets and finds out surplus and deficit cash position of the period.
options.B: Cash budget integrates all capital budgets and finds out surplus and deficit cash position of the period.
options.D: Cash budget integrates all operating budgets and finds out surplus and deficit cash position of the period.

questions.explanation: The cash budget fundamentally maps cash inflows and outflows by integrating information mapped out in the various operating budgets (like sales, purchases, labour, etc.) to determine the cash surplus or deficit position of the period.

questions.question_text: Find the material cost variance from the information given below: Budgeted Production: 1000 units; Each unit requires 5 Kgs of Material and each KG of material costs Rs. 10 per KG. Actual Production: 800 units. Material procured is 4500 Kgs at Rs. 12 per KG.
questions.explanation:
Standard Quantity for Actual Production = 800 units × 5 Kgs/unit = 4000 KGs.
Standard Cost for Actual Production = 4000 KGs × Rs. 10 = Rs. 40000.
Actual Cost = Actual Quantity × Actual Price = 4500 KGs × Rs. 12 = Rs. 54000.
Material Cost Variance = Standard Cost - Actual Cost = 40000 - 54000 = -14000 (Adverse).

questions.question_text: Find the material price variance (Rate Variance) from the information given below: Budgeted Production: 1000 units; Each unit requires 5 Kgs of Material and each KG of material costs Rs. 10 per KG. Actual Production: 800 units. Material procured is 4500 Kgs at Rs. 12 per KG.
questions.explanation:
Material Price Variance = (Standard Price - Actual Price) × Actual Quantity.
Standard Price = Rs. 10.
Actual Price = Rs. 12.
Actual Quantity = 4500 KGs.
Material Price Variance = (10 - 12) × 4500 = -2 × 4500 = -9000 (Adverse).

questions.question_text: Find the material usage variance (Efficiency Variance) from the information given below: Budgeted Production: 1000 units; Each unit requires 5 Kgs of Material and each KG of material costs Rs. 10 per KG. Actual Production: 800 units. Material procured is 4500 Kgs at Rs. 12 per KG.
questions.explanation:
Standard Quantity (SQ) for Actual Production = 800 units × 5 Kgs/unit = 4000 KGs.
Actual Quantity (AQ) used = 4500 KGs.
Standard Price (SP) = Rs. 10 per KG.
Material Usage Variance = (SQ - AQ) × SP = (4000 - 4500) × 10 = -500 × 10 = -5000 (Adverse).

questions.question_text: Chocorp' budgeted sales for its premier chocolate for the first quarter was 10,00,000 units at the rate of Rs. 100 per unit. The actual sales was 12,00,000 units and the average price realization was Rs. 95. Find the sales variance and its components (Rate Variance; Quantity Variance; Total Sales Variance).

options.A: Rate Variance: Rs. 60 Lakhs (Adverse); Quantity Variance: Rs. 200 lakhs (Favourable); Total Sales Variance: Rs. 140 Lakhs (Favourable)
options.B: Rate Variance: Rs. 50 Lakhs (Favourable); Quantity Variance: Rs. 240 lakhs (Adverse); Total Sales Variance: Rs. 190 Lakhs (Adverse)
options.C: Rate Variance: Rs. 60 Lakhs (Favourable); Quantity Variance: Rs. 200 lakhs (Adverse); Total Sales Variance: Rs. 140 Lakhs (Adverse)
options.D: Rate Variance: Rs. 50 Lakhs (Adverse); Quantity Variance: Rs. 240 lakhs (Favourable); Total Sales Variance: Rs. 190 Lakhs (Favourable)

questions.explanation:
Budgeted Sales Value = 10,00,000 units × Rs. 100 = Rs. 1000 Lakhs.
Actual Sales Value = 12,00,000 units × Rs. 95 = Rs. 1140 Lakhs.
Total Sales Variance = Actual Sales - Budgeted Sales = 1140 - 1000 = +140 Lakhs (Favourable).
Sales Rate (Price) Variance = (Actual Price - Standard Price) × Actual Quantity = (95 - 100) × 12,00,000 = -60 Lakhs (Adverse).
Sales Quantity (Volume) Variance = (Actual Quantity - Standard Quantity) × Standard Price = (12,00,000 - 10,00,000) × 100 = +200 Lakhs (Favourable).
